2019_132_041619regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of April 16, 2019 at the Services Building. It recognizes 43 nominees for the Outstanding Teacher Award — with Zach Rondot of Costello named both TSD and Oakland County Elementary Teacher of the Year and Josh Pudaloff of Athens named Overall TSD Teacher of the Year — carries the February 2019 Treasurer's Report showing total disbursements in period of $10,632,328.69, sells a 720-square-foot parcel on Boyd Street to Delmar Homes for $10,000.00, and awards $110,000.00 of interior painting and a $101,760.00 bathroom partition replacement.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, April 16, 2019, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Agenda: Pledge; Recognition; Additions & Deletions; Public Communication; General – Consent Agenda; Personnel; Curriculum; Business; Public Communication (non-agenda); Other; Adjournment.

**Recognition**
The Mission Moment recognizes Martell Elementary students for embracing "Character," one of the six C's of deep learning; principal Michelle Barsh introduces Anastasia Kulikowska, Anshika Sharm and Riley Durak, who present what character means to them. The Outstanding Teacher item honors 43 nominees drawn from every level, nominated by peers, parents and students — 40 recognized with certificates and plants, and three sent to Oakland Schools for the county-wide program: Zach Rondot, a 4th grade teacher at Costello Elementary, named TSD Elementary School Teacher of the Year and Oakland County Elementary Teacher of the Year; Sue Domin, a 7th grade teacher at Boulan Park, named TSD Middle School Teacher of the Year; and Josh Pudaloff, computer science teacher at Athens, named both TSD High School Teacher of the Year and Overall TSD Teacher of the Year.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the March 5 workshop and March 19 meeting, the February 2019 Treasurer's Report, the Boyd Street property purchase agreement, and an amendment to the March site work projects resolution.

**Treasurer's Report — February 2019**
Check disbursements total $8,356,284.91 — General Fund $6,257,543.07, Special Revenue Funds $142,503.75 and Other Funds $1,956,238.09 — with ACH debits of $16,284.94, outgoing wire transfers of $2,067,346.27, P-Card purchases of $194,731.75 and prior period voids of ($2,319.18), giving total disbursements in period of $10,632,328.69. Capital Projects Funds account for 1,848,395.36 of the check total. At February 28, 2019 the General Fund balance stands at $29,659,434, Debt Service at $14,960,240 and consolidated Special Revenue at $2,675,496.

**What the March minutes record**
The March 5 workshop, held at the Troy Center for Transition/IA-East with Clark Hill attorney Dana Abrams present, covered a Section 1 update, the 1:1 high school pilot review, districtwide site work and asbestos abatement, the 2019 school building and site bonds, an ancillary funds budget amendment, preschool technology cabling and aquatic sports timing equipment.

The March 19 meeting recognized Amogh Gowda, a Troy High junior and distinguished finalist for the Prudential Spirit of Community Award for developing an organ donation awareness program as a certified Gift of Life Michigan volunteer, and honored Wass Elementary as a 2019 State School of Character — its application forwarded for National School of Character consideration — with Wattles named an Honorable Mention and Athens recognized as Emerging; Character.org's Michigan coordinator Lori Soifer presented the certificate to Wass principal Matt Jansen. The Board then passed a series of 7-0 resolutions: districtwide site work to Asphalt Specialists, Inc. at $822,140.00 from the Building and Site Sinking Fund; districtwide asbestos abatement to Trust Thermal Abatement at $288,420.00; authorization to issue **2019 School Building and Site Bonds in an amount not to exceed $27,000,000**; preschool cabling infrastructure to Complete Interactive Technologies at $59,905.31; aquatic sports timing equipment to Riegle Timing Consultants LLC at $65,008.00; cancellation of the June 18, 2019 meeting; and, under Public Acts 435, 538, 549 and 670 of 2018, designation of a school safety liaison to the new Office of School Safety and an emergency contact for the Attorney General's hotline, both to be reported to the Department of State Police by March 28, 2019.

**Business**
The Boyd Street resolution sells a 720-square-foot strip in Section 23 — a six-foot extension along the northerly line of Beaver Run Subdivision — to Delmar Homes for $10,000.00, and rescinds the earlier sale resolution adopted November 20, 2018. The site work amendment adds the 2016 Capital Projects Fund as a second funding source for the $822,140.00 Asphalt Specialists award, which had been funded solely from the Building and Site Sinking Fund.

Interior painting at eight buildings is awarded at $110,000.00 from the Capital Maintenance Fund, split between RNC Paint Systems at $32,541.60 and General Painting Co., LLC at $50,830.00 with $26,628.40 held as contingency for future needs; the BID 9883 tabulation shows total bids ranging from $81,250.00 to $200,158.00 across five painters. The bathroom partition replacement project at Athens, Troy High, Boulan Park and Larson is awarded to Leggette Co. at $101,760.00 from the Building and Site Sinking Fund.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, April 16, 2019, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition — A. TSD Mission Moment: Martell Elementary Students Embrace "Character", B. Troy School District's Outstanding Teachers; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum; 8. Business; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment.

**Recognition.** The Mission Moment recognizes students from Martell Elementary School for embracing "Character," one of the six C's of deep learning; three Martell students attend to share a presentation they created on what character means to them, introduced by principal Michelle Barsh — Anastasia Kulikowska, Anshika Sharm and Riley Durak.

Item 2.B covers the Oakland County Outstanding Teacher of the Year Awards. The district recognizes 43 individuals nominated for the Troy School District Outstanding Teacher Award Program, representing exemplary educators at the elementary, middle and high school levels, nominated by peers, parents and students, whose nomination letters described how they go above and beyond to ensure students learn, grow and thrive. Forty nominees are honored with certificates and plants: Ruba Alexander (Wattles/Troy Union Elementary), Eric Andary (Troy Union Elementary), Ping Bai (Baker Middle School), Janice Boyer (Hamilton Elementary), Kerry Brennan (Smith Middle School), Karen Bush (Schroeder Elementary), Sharon Callas (Costello Elementary), Angela Clemence (Wattles Elementary), Nicole Coffer (Barnard Elementary), Genia Connell (Leonard Elementary), Scott Crecelius (Larson Middle School), Lisa Danhoff (Troy High School), Danielle Davenport (Hill Elementary), Kelsey Drabik (Wattles Elementary), Karie Dunneback (Athens High School), Julie Eldridge (Costello Elementary), Angelika Gadlage (Bemis Elementary), Nancy Haboush (Leonard Elementary), Jamie Hallmark (International Academy East), Sara Jozefiak (Barnard Elementary), Deborah Kellett (Wass Elementary), Sandy Koneval (Boulan Park Middle School), Joan Levitt (Boulan Park Middle School), Lindsey Maliepaard (Costello Elementary), Tim Marley (Troy High School), Mark Martin (Boulan Park Middle School), Cara McKeever (Hamilton Elementary), Amy Mee (Leonard/Hill Elementary), Sherri Parks (Troy High School), Karen Reese (Costello Elementary), Carol Rexer (Larson Middle School), Jennifer Sobczynski (Troy High School), Kathryn Starn (Leonard Elementary), Matthew Tignanelli (Morse Elementary), Jaclyn Toepel-Hartzell (International Academy East), Ray Torres (Smith Middle School), Lyndsey Versteegden (Morse Elementary), Katie Vitale (Troy High School), Amy Wallace (Leonard Elementary) and Audrey Wright (Boulan Park Middle School). Three district nominees went forward to Oakland Schools for the county-wide program: Zach Rondot, 4th Grade Teacher at Costello Elementary School, named TSD Elementary School Teacher of the Year and Oakland County Elementary Teacher of the Year; Sue Domin, 7th Grade Teacher at Boulan Park Middle School, named TSD Middle School Teacher of the Year; and Josh Pudaloff, Computer Science Teacher at Athens High School, named TSD High School Teacher of the Year and Overall TSD Teacher of the Year. All three are invited to speak.

**Consent agenda.** A. Minutes of the March 5, 2019 workshop; B. Minutes of the March 19, 2019 meeting; C. Treasurer's Report for February 2019; D. Boyd St. Property; and E. March Site Work Projects Resolution Amendment.

**March 5, 2019 workshop minutes.** President Schmidt called the workshop to order at 6:15 p.m. at the Troy Center for Transition/IA-East, 1291 Torpey Drive, with Mrs. Fleming, Mr. Gottlieb, Mrs. Hammond, Mr. Hauff, Dr. Philippart and Dr. Wilson present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Carson, Carrier, Gottlieb, Griffor, Harris, Soggs and West, and Clark Hill attorney Dana Abrams, with nine students in the audience. The agenda covered public communication; a Section 1 update; a Teaching and Learning update including the 1:1 high school pilot review; a Business Services update covering districtwide site work projects, districtwide asbestos abatement, the 2019 school building and site bonds, an ancillary funds budget amendment, the Troy Preschool technology cabling bid and aquatic sports timing equipment for Athens; and the June 18, 2019 board meeting. It adjourned at 9:30 p.m., Gary N. Hauff signing as Secretary.

**March 19, 2019 meeting minutes.** President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. at the Services Building with Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present, Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, Cross, Jansen, Brasington, Dixon, Roncone, Griffor, Harris and West in attendance, and approximately 100 members of the audience.

The Mission Moment recognized Amogh Gowda, a junior at Troy High School and a distinguished finalist for the Prudential Spirit of Community Award for developing an awareness program on organ donation; he is a certified volunteer for Gift of Life Michigan who speaks at venues and volunteers at community events to empower youth and promote the fact that one organ donor can save up to eight lives. The Board also honored Wass Elementary School as a 2019 State School of Character, an award given to a select few schools each year for implementing 11 core principles including promoting good character, culture and ethics, fostering student self-motivation, giving students opportunity for moral action, and engaging families and community members as partners in character-building; Wass was praised for high quality work in all 11 principle areas and its application was forwarded for consideration as a National School of Character. Wattles Elementary was commended as a 2019 Honorable Mention School of Character and Athens High School was recognized as Emerging. Lori Soifer, Character.org Coordinator for the State of Michigan, presented the official certificate to Matt Jansen, Principal of Wass Elementary.

In public communication, Pietro Sarcina, a Troy resident, addressed the Board regarding the removal of the tennis courts at all middle schools in the District. Resolution 19-027 approved the consent agenda: minutes of the February 5, 2019 workshop, minutes of the February 26, 2019 meeting, the Treasurer's Report for January 2019, and an ancillary funds budget amendment. Resolution 19-028 approved the personnel recommendation, new hire Erin Mullins. Under business, resolution 19-029 awarded districtwide site work projects to Asphalt Specialists, Inc. in the amount of $822,140.00 as an expenditure of the Building and Site Sinking Fund; 19-030 awarded districtwide asbestos abatement to Trust Thermal Abatement in the amount of $288,420.00 from the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and the Building and Site Sinking Fund; and 19-031 authorized the issuance of bonds designated the "2019 School Building and Site Bonds" in an amount not to exceed $27,000,000, with the full resolution made part of the official minutes of the March 19, 2019 regular meeting. Resolution 19-032 awarded cabling infrastructure for the Troy School District Preschool to Complete Interactive Technologies in the amount of $59,905.31 from the Early Childhood Center Fund, and 19-033 awarded aquatic sports timing equipment and installation to Riegle Timing Consultants LLC in the amount of $65,008.00 from the General Fund and Activity Fund. Resolution 19-034 cancelled the June 18, 2019 Board of Education meeting.

Resolution 19-035 designated a school safety liaison and emergency contact. It recites that Public Act 435 of 2018 establishes the Office of School Safety within the Department of State Police, tasked with working with the Michigan Department of Education to create model practices for school safety and offering school safety trainings; that Public Act 538 of 2018 requires the Department of State Police to create a School Safety Commission to review model practices and make policy recommendations; that Public Act 549 of 2018 requires the Board to designate a district employee as liaison to both bodies, who must regularly and continuously work under contract for the district; that under the Student Safety Act, MCL 752.913(3), the Attorney General operates a hotline for reports regarding potential self-harm and potential harm or criminal acts directed at school students, employees or schools in Michigan; and that Public Act 670 of 2018 requires the governing body to provide the Department of State Police, at least biannually, with current emergency contact information for at least one school official able to receive hotline information. It directs the Superintendent to designate the liaison and notify the Department of State Police by March 28, 2019, and to provide the contact information of at least one school official to receive information from the Attorney General's hotline by the same date. Every vote that evening was 7 yes, 0 no. Gary N. Hauff certified the resolution and that notice was given under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267 of the Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Treasurer's Report, February 2019.** Rick West certifies the disbursements. Capital Projects Funds (414, 416, 418, 498, 499) account for 1,848,395.36 and the Student Activity Fund (700, 701) for 107,842.73, with Facility Rentals, Debt Funds and the Memorial Scholarship Fund at none. Totals are General Fund $6,257,543.07, Special Revenue Funds $142,503.75 and Other Funds $1,956,238.09, for total check disbursements of $8,356,284.91; with ACH debits of $16,284.94, outgoing wire transfers of $2,067,346.27, P-Card purchases of $194,731.75 and prior period void disbursements of ($2,319.18), total disbursements in period are $10,632,328.69. The summary budget reports for the period July 1, 2018 through February 28, 2019 give a General Fund balance of $29,659,434, a consolidated Debt Service balance of $14,960,240 and a consolidated Special Revenue balance of $2,675,496.

**Consent item 5.D: Boyd Street property.** The resolution recites that the district desires to sell a parcel described as part of the Northeast 1/4 of the Southwest 1/4 of Section 23, Town 2 North, Range 11 East, City of Troy, Oakland County, beginning at the northwest corner of Lot 28 of "Beaver Run Subdivision" as recorded in Liber 46 of Plats on Page 27, running northerly 6.00 feet on the extension of the westerly line of Lot 28, easterly 120.00 feet parallel to the northerly line of the subdivision, southerly 6.00 feet along the northerly extension of the easterly line of Lot 29, and westerly 120.00 feet back to the point of beginning — containing 720 square feet. The district received an Offer To Purchase from Delmar Homes for a purchase price of Ten Thousand and 00/100 ($10,000.00) Dollars. The resolution authorizes the sale on terms substantially similar to the attached Offer, authorizes the Superintendent or designee to execute it and any incidental documents, and rescinds the resolution approving the sale of the Boyd St. Property adopted at the November 20, 2018 Board of Education meeting.

**Consent item 5.E: site work projects amendment.** The Board approved a resolution in March 2019 for districtwide sitework projects funded from the Building and Site Sinking Fund; the amendment adds the 2016 Capital Projects Fund as an additional funding source for the same $822,140.00 award to Asphalt Specialists, Inc.

**Business 8.A: interior painting.** An RFP sought competitive bids for interior painting at various school buildings, with responses reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Operations, Katelyn Weaver and Michelle Kerns. The resolution awards interior painting in the amount of $110,000.00 as an expenditure of the Capital Maintenance Fund, with the resolution made part of the official minutes of the April 16, 2019 regular meeting. The award splits between RNC Paint Systems at $32,541.60 and General Painting Co., LLC at $50,830.00, with $26,628.40 held as contingency for future needs. The BID 9883 tabulation, dated 4/11/2019, covers Barnard, Costello, Hamilton, Hill, Leonard and Martell elementary schools, Smith Middle School and Troy High School, listing per-building prices and bond costs for five bidders: RNC Paint Systems at a $90,284.00 total bid, General Painting Co., LLC at $81,250.00, Paint Plus at $200,158.00, Jarvis Painting, Inc. at $122,932.00 and Seven Brothers Painting, Inc. at $137,161.00.

**Business 8.B: bathroom partition replacement.** An RFP was issued for the bathroom partition replacement project at Athens, Troy High, Boulan Park and Larson middle and high schools, with responses reviewed by Rob Carson. The RFP produced three bids with R.E. Leggette Co. the apparent low bidder, and the resolution awards the project to Leggette Co. in the amount of $101,760.00 as an expenditure of the Building and Site Sinking Fund.
